title: Ensminger, Monroy each score twice as Warriors romp in opener for new head coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Ensminger, Monroy each score twice as Warriors romp in opener for new head coach

 September 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 600
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — He knows there will be tougher games and stiffer competition.But, man, did this first one feel good.
Kyle Ensminger scored a pair of goals in the opening 14 minutes, and Ale Monroy scored in each half Tuesday, as Easton High's boys soccer team rolled to an 8-0 victory over Wicomico in the head coaching debut of Avery Brice.
"Feels great," said Brice, who played on the Warriors' 2014 team that reached the Class 2A state championship game. "I told the guys in the group, everything I asked of them they delivered. I think that means a lot for me. It means they're balled in. They got the same mindset as me. That means everything. First game, 8-0. But it doesn't stop today. And we don't be complacent."
Ensminger collected a pass from Kai Ferraris, slipped past a defender, and deposited Easton's first goal of the season into the net just 4:14 into the game.
Wicomico keeper Matthew Bier stopped a point-blank bid by Ensminger a little over two minutes later. But in the 14th minute, Ensminger gathered a lead pass from Dominic Stanco, calmly pushed downfield with a pair of defenders closing on his right hip, drew Bier off his line, and neatly tucked a left-footed shot into the right side of the net for a 2-0 lead.
The Warriors continued to extend their advantage.
Mario Medina fed Monroy, who unloaded a low, hard drive off Bier's hands for a 3-0 cushion with 25:30 left in the first half. CJ Chaconas settled a ball from Ensminger and hammered a shot off the keeper's hands to make it 4-0. Landon Chaney capped the first-half scoring with a drive from near the left post for a 5-0 Warrior lead.
"We continue to go," said Brice of his team's not getting complacent despite its comfortable halftime lead. "And I know when we get really tested, opportunities won't come like they did today. I told the guys that. So we do got to work on finishing, things of that nature, taking our chances and making them count when they are presented upon us."
Easton junior keeper Sam Hutchison was never seriously challenged, as the Warriors' backline and midfield controlled play.
"Love our defense. Love our possession game," Brice said. "The guys know that we got to play a little bit simpler. And I told the guys from the get (go), like we do the simple things correct, we'll be the best team."
Medina broke in from left wing in the 8th minute of the second half and was taken down, setting up his penalty-kick goal that pushed the lead to 6-0. Monroy netted his second goal with an innocent-looking chip less than two minutes later. Elmer Pineda completed with scoring with 24:08 remaining when he put one past Indians backup keeper Sam Fleuriot, making it 8-0.
A new rule instituted this season stops play in the 60th minute if a team has an eight-goal lead.
"It was the first thing I was thinking when I woke up this morning," Brice said of his first game as head coach. "So proud of these guys. Talented team. I just want them to continue to know that. One game at a time. We move on. OK, it's not a celebration. We did what we were supposed to and we move on."
QUEEN ANNE'S 2, PARKSIDE 2
CENTREVILLE — Ryan Lee and James Rath each scored once, and Gage Jordan notched an assist as the Lions battled the Rams to a draw in double overtime.
J.M. BENNETT 10, N. CAROLINE 2
RIDGELY — Heath Frantum and Ayden Russell had one goal apiece for the Bulldogs against the defending Bayside Conference-champion Clippers.

title: Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's takes aim at fifth straight North Bayside title and more

 September 19, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1297
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Queen Anne's County High's girls soccer program has compiled an impressive resume during Mike Kern's 23 seasons as head coach.The Lions have won 14 North Bayside titles and two Bayside Conference championships. They've reached 11 regional finals, winning twice, and have advanced to the state finals once.
But as Queen Anne's has worked through preseason tryouts, scrimmages and into the regular season's early weeks, Kern sees a team that could be among his finest from front to back.
"This might be our most talented team we've ever had in my opinion," said Kern, who has never had a losing record as he enters his 24th season as head coach. "Every single one of them has played travel for years. There's a lot of times we'd get good athletes that played lacrosse or something else, and just played soccer to stay in shape. But this year we have soccer players. And for most of the girls, their first sport is soccer. I think that's the difference from years past."
Despite that talent, which includes all-state first-team selection and returning North Bayside Player of the Year Olivia Ryan, Kern knows there is one main obstacle in his team's path to a fifth consecutive North title — the 2020 COVID-shortened season excluded — and a potential regional title — Kent Island.
Though Queen Anne's shut out the Bucs 3-0 during the regular season last year, it lost 3-2 in double overtime in the Class 2A East Region II title game.
The Lions blanked Kent Island, 1-0, already this season, but have a second date with their county rival Oct. 16 which will likely decided the division crown, and then could have a third encounter come the postseason.
"I'm excited. I really am," Kern said of the season. "We should go far. But we've got to get through Kent Island."
Here's a look at this year's teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SDHead Coach: Sarah Alpaugh.
Who's Where: Goalie: Akizhae Hammond (Jr.); Backs: Monti Jackson (So.); Skyla Ali (So.); Mimi Exume (So.); Sophia Diaz (Fr.); Midfield: Lainey Jones (Sr.); Olivia Fischer (Fr.); Kamryn Bourne (So.); Lilly Moxey (Fr.); Forwards: Laila Insley (Sr.); Madalyn Spicer (Jr.); Jade Bryant (Jr.); Kennedy Bourne (So.).
Outlook: The Vikings graduated their entire defensive unit from a year ago, so one of Alpaugh's focuses will be hoping a young cast of replacements can stick together and gain experience to form a strong foundation for the future.
Jones is a four-year starter that anchors a midfield, which hopes to regain the services of returning starter Kamryn Bourne, who was injured in the season's second game. Alpaugh, who begins her third year, calls Insley a key component, and coupled with the speedy Bryant, could provide a nice one-two punch at the top.
COL. RICHARDSONHead Coach: Beth Carmen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cloee Welzel (So.); Backs: Olivia McGregor (So.); Kallie Peele (Sr.); Violet Cheezum (Jr.); Adan Alvi (Sr.); Agatha Divjak (Fr.); Lila Schriefer (Jr.); Vanessa Odidika (Sr.); Midfield: Brynne Harper (So.); Doranelli Tomas-Ortiz (So.); Forwards: Ryleigh Hall (So.); Sadie Prettyman (So.).
Outlook: The Colonels got clobbered by Snow Hill a year ago, 8-0. They met the Eagles in this year's opener and scored the game's first goal in an eventual 4-2 loss.
"I have really seen a lot of improvement from last year," said Carmen, who is in her second year as head coach. "I've actually had one of the refs come over to me and say this is one of the best looking Colonel girls soccer teams that he's seen in a long time."
Carmen will rotate players between defense and midfield, and attack and midfield in hopes of finding a consistent combination. After falling to the Eagles in the opener, Colonel bounced back with wins over Cambridge-SD and North Dorchester.
"This is a really great group of kids," Carmen said. "They work well together and they communicate well."
EASTONHead Coach: Ellie Kilmon.
Who's Where: Goalie Zelia Proa (So.); Backs: Dakota Lhotsky (Jr.); Sam Murphy (Sr.); Bella Swann (Sr.); Finley Golden (So.); Stella Petrichenko (So.); Midfield: Addie Schindler (Fr.); Laillah Janes (Sr.); Addie Chandler (Sr.); Anna Quidley (Sr.); Megan Wright (Fr.); Angie Martinez (Jr.); Forward: Miranda Stup (Jr.).
Outlook: Kilmon isn't making any predictions whether the Warriors can battle Queen Anne's and Kent Island for division supremacy.
"I never know until we play," Kilmon said. "It really depends on how the girls show up and play."
Center backs Lhotsky and Murphy look to provide a solid defensive core.
"I'm excited for the year," Kilmon said. "I think we have a good amount of returners and we just have a nice team dynamics that's building so I'm excited to seem them grow together."
KENT COUNTYHead Coach: Ben Joiner.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sophia Cousineau (So.); Backs: Mary Jane Joiner (Jr.); Paige Miller (Sr.); Savanna Reynolds (Jr.); Reese Strong (Fr.); Midfield: Delilah Markovic (Jr.); Jane Cleary (So.); Emy Karlik (Fr.); Bella Hinefelt (So.); Forwards: Zuleika Nava (Jr.); Sabrina Tee (Fr.); Madison Garcia (Fr.); Morgan Kendall (Sr.); Kayla Aguilar (Fr.); Ashlynn Elborn (Fr.); Amelia Plummer (Fr.).
Outlook: A 1995 Kent County graduate, Joiner takes over as head coach and has watched his young team get off to a 2-1 start.
"We really got a lot of positive momentum going with the number of girls that have joined the team this year," said Joiner, who praised the work of assistant Joel Tolbert in helping develop the team. "We're super young. We're really relying on the leadership of our seniors and juniors to elevate the team."
Joiner said an emphasis has been placed on defense in preparation for the 2A schools on the schedule, but has been encouraged by his team's play against 1A rivals.
NORTH CAROLINEHead Coach: Jenna Riordan.
Who's Where: Goalie: Rylee Gowen (Jr.); Amber Biars (Jr.); Backs: Sarah Brown (Sr.); Natalie Newman (Jr.); Izzy Knott (Sr.); Midfield: Emma Hansley (So.); Megan Rogers (Sr.); Madison McNinch (Jr.); Paisley Garland (Jr.); Linda Ridgell (Jr.); Forwards: Irma Sanchez (Jr.); Seanna Rupp (Sr.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs opened the season by defeating Parkside — gaining a measure of revenge on the Rams, who knocked them out of the playoffs in last year's 2A East Region I title game — but then lost by a goal to Easton before getting humbled by Stephen Decatur.
"We have had a rough start to our season so far, but I'm hoping to get a couple wins under our belts the next two weeks," Riordan said. "That ought to help our record."
Riordan also hopes a few wins help her team's confidence as it transitions from a 4-4-2 scheme to a 3-5-2 alignment.
"We're still adjusting and learning our positions," said Riordan, who begins her sixth season. "I've always said that we play up to the teams that are above us, so I do think we'll play (Queen Anne's and Kent Island) a really good game."
QUEEN ANNE'SHead Coach: Mike Kern.
Who's Where: Goalie: Bea Holthaus (So.); Backs: Shannon Rath (Jr.); Hayden Legg (Sr.); Finley Patchett (So.); Kathryn Baer (Sr.); Abby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Chloe Sharp (Sr.); Olivia Ryan (Sr.); Morgan Scott (Sr.); Kara Ringold (Jr.); Forwards: Madi Horney (So.); Riley Klepper (Sr.); Taylor Napier (So.).
Outlook: The most notable graduation loss for the Lions was back Elizabeth Oldfield. But this could be one of the best defensive units Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have ever had in Centreville.
Kern also noted Scott and Ringold may be the two best outside midfielders Queen Anne's has had since the days of former standout Kesley Dean. Add to the mix Ryan, the all-state pick and the Lions' leading scorer from last year is back, along with a group of nine sophomores, several of which played together on a travel team coached by Kern.
Despite all that, Kent Island remains the primary hurdle in the North, while James M. Bennett or Stephen Decatur — which defeated the Lions in overtime to open the season — are angling toward the South Bayside crown and a possible conference championship showdown.
Editor's Note: Information for Kent Island and North Dorchester was unavailable.

title: Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints

 September 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 708
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Johnny Mautz hadn't played high school soccer before this season.Judging by the celebration he triggered midway through Tuesday night's second half, his St. Michaels High teammates are elated he decided to give the game a go this season.
Ethan Royer crossed a ball that Mautz converted into what proved to be the game-winning goal, as the Saints rallied from a halftime deficit to notch a 3-2 victory over Class 1A rival and previously unbeaten Colonel Richardson.
"I was playing baseball for awhile but I just stopped playing last year," said Mautz, a standout on the Saints' basketball team. "I never played soccer 'cause I didn't want to play three sports. But I said I might as well come out because I was only playing one sport (basketball). And then the rest is history."
There was also a touch of history attached to Mautz' score.
"That was his first goal of the year," St. Michaels head coach Pat Hambleton said of Mautz. "He's hit the post six times."
That strike with 21 minutes, 9 seconds remaining not only capped a three-goal, second-half surge, giving St. Michaels a 3-1 lead, but it also afforded the Saints (3-2 overall, 2-1 North Bayside) the breathing room they needed to weather Colonels' late-game push.
Not quite 4 minutes after having a goal erased by an offsides call, Colonel (4-1, 2-1) took a 1-0 lead on Aydan Downie's unassisted tally with 9:42 left in the first half.
St. Michaels' best chance to pull even came with just under 2 minutes to go in the first half, when Miles Fox put a shot right on Colonel keeper Cohen Carels, who made a midsection stop.
The Saints pulled even though just 1:26 into the second half, when Sherwin Mendez parked a direct kick into the back of the net for a 1-all tie.
"I think their free kick a minute and a half into the second half definitely gave them some momentum," Colonel head coach Dillon Shaheen said. "And they took that and ran with it."
Not quite 10 minutes later, Fox got deep on the left wing and steered a crossing pass that Connor Wheeler banged into the net for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
"Their sweeper was playing a little too far back I noticed," Hambleton said. "He was solely intercepting through balls, so I just made a small adjustment, where once he left for that through ball, I had a forward there, and it happened to be Connor. So he left, peeled off to Miles. Miles received and played that ball across, and it was wide open in the front of the net. It was just a good momentum boost that we needed to start the half."
Less than 8 minutes later, Royer slid a pass from the left side through the crease to the right post and a waiting Mautz for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been working on staying back post so that I can get whatever comes my way," Mautz said. "And Ethan played me a beautiful ball and I was just right there for the lefty finish."
Colonel wasn't quite finished though.
With 15:06 remaining, St. Michaels was called for a handball in the box. Colonel's Angel Castro Rios calmly deposited the penalty kick to the left of St. Michaels keeper Lucas Greenwood to make it a one-goal difference.
With Colonel continuing to push into the Saints' end, Hambleton dropped his team into defensive mode. St. Michaels foiled rushes and generally got in the way over the final 12 minutes, with Colonel's best chance for the equalizer coming with 6:37 left, when Greenwood smothered a loose ball near the left post in front of a charging Downie.
"Energy. They definitely came out a little more ready than we were, and we talked to them about that at halftime," Shaheen said. "I think they wanted the ball more it seemed. We match up pretty well with them, and they know they match up well with us. What it usually comes down to is which ever team plays harder, and they were definitely that team."
NORTH CAROLINE 8 CAMBRIDGE-SD 0
CAMBRIDGE — Omar Marroquin had a hat trick as the Bulldogs earned their first win of the season.
North Caroline (1-4, 1-2) also got goals from Mason Shilling, Adrian Lopez Rivera, Brayden Boarts, Karson Hollingworth and Jimmy Cohoon.

title: Bennett blanks Queen Anne's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bennett blanks Queen Anne's

 October 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 751
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Mike Kern tried stopping them before they started."Don't hang your heads," Queen Anne's County High's girls head soccer coach instructed his players after Monday night's 3-0 loss to James M. Bennett.
Though the defending Bayside Conference-champion Clippers had ended the Lions' five-game winning streak, Kern was encouraged by what he saw.
"It's great playing against good competition," said Kern, whose team had outscored its last five opponents 29-0. "I thought we played well."
Queen Anne's (5-2) had also come within inches of playing even with Bennett (7-0) until late in the second half.
Chloe Sharp sent a header wide right midway through the first half. Shannon Rath unloaded a rocket into the left side of the net less than a minute later, but it was waved off because it came on an indirect kick.
"We had our chances," Kern said.
And the Lions would create more chances.
But it was the Clippers who were able to finish their opportunities.
The first of those came with 15 minutes, 41 seconds left in the first half, when a Bennett corner kick slipped behind Queen Anne's keeper Bea Holthaus. Queen Anne's Ava Bouch converged on the ball between Bennett's Gracie Core and Isabella Wieland. But Core, a freshman striker, arrived at the ball first, and poked the game's first score in with her left foot.
"We had two breakdowns," Kern said. "One on the corner kick; we really didn't go to the ball well. The ball bounced around the middle and they snuck it in. It was unfortunate, but we've got to do a better job of winning the ball there."
Bennett widened its lead to 2-0 with 4:43 left in the first half, as Riley Matthews gained possession, came down left wing, and angled a hard shot that eluded Holthaus' lunge before settling into the right side of the goal.
"We shoot on sight," Bennett head coach Ed O'Leary said. "When we get in front of the goal, when we get a chance, we get on target a lot. And that's what I think the difference was."
The Lions just missed trimming that two-goal deficit with 3:10 remaining in the first half, when Sharp unloaded a drive that banged off the crossbar, but fell just in front of the goal line.
Sharp rang yet another ball off the crossbar 50 seconds into the second half.
Holthaus kept it a two-goal game, stopping a Matthews' shot from left wing 3 minutes into the second half, then tracking a 30-yard direct kick for another save less than 2 minutes later.
Madi Horny had Queen Anne's two last scoring chances, angling a ball from right wing toward the left post that Valenzano smothered with 18:20 left. Valenzano stopped yet another Horney chance a little more than 3 minutes later.
"We got to score against good teams," Kern said. "We've got to get the ball in the back of the net. We were creating some opportunities, but we got to finish."
Matthews finished yet another chance with 6:28 remaining, when she got a thru pass from Core, broke down the left side alone against Holthaus and parked a shot into the left side for a 3-0 lead.
"That's what we can't have," Kern said of Matthews' breakaway. "We've got to keep them in front, and that's kind of what we stress. We did a good job with that most of the game except for that one play.
"But at the end there we pushed Shannon (Rath) up," Kern said. "We had some opportunities. We were attacking and had a lot of momentum going. And then they got that one little breakaway that sealed the game for them."
The three-goal victory was the Clippers' narrowest margin of victory this season, matching their 4-1 win over Kent Island on Sept. 16. Bennett had outscored its other five opponents, 40-1.
"We've kind of had an easy start," O'Leary said. "Kent Island was a tough game for us, but this was our big test. We were looking forward to it. Teams coached by coach Kern, they're always physical and they're always skillful and they're motivated. So for us to come out here and win this. ... I think 3-0 is a bit flattering, but it was a good tough game and we needed it.
"It's going to do us a world of good going forward," O'Leary added. "Just proud. They pinned us back into our half a few times and we stood tall and we played hard and we didn't concede a goal and got through. Some days it's your day, and some days it's not. Today was our day."

title: Warriors battle but can’t extend win streak against undefeated Bennett
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors battle but can’t extend win streak against undefeated Bennett

 October 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 714
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Avery Brice was eager for Monday night."I was very excited about this game tonight just to see where we were at as far as playing against top competition," Easton High's first-year boys head soccer coach said of facing undefeated and defending Bayside Conference champion James M. Bennett.
After 80 minutes, the Warriors were where everyone else has been this season after playing the Clippers — behind on the scoreboard.
And yet despite watching Easton's four-game win streak come to a halt in a 3-0 loss, Brice was largely encouraged by what he saw from his team.
"Goals change momentum," said Brice, who watched the Clippers take a 1-0 lead, when star Noah Blankensop gained possession on left wing, and, with Easton keeper Sam Hutchison far from his goal, sent a ball drifting over everyone before settling into the right side of the net with 15 minutes, 27 seconds left in the first half. "I loved how we responded. Going down a goal sucks. Guys responded great. Better than we have previously. We get scored on and it's like, 'Wow.' You just see everyone drop. But tonight you saw guys, 'Hey come on. Next play. Let's go again.' I was really proud of them for that."
Brice was also proud of Hutchison's play in goal. The junior keeper stopped a hard shot by Blankensop in the 9th minute and made a save on Sebastien Dorvelus just a moment later to keep the game scoreless. Hutchison then made perhaps his stop of the game, when he punched away a shot that banged off the left post with 7 minutes left in the first half, keeping it a one-goal game.
"Goalie had a huge night," Brice said of Hutchison, who finished with 11 saves. "Crazy saves. One of the best games I've seen him play."
Bennett (8-0), which has beaten six of its eight opponents this season by six or more goals — the exceptions, Queen Anne's (3-0 on Sept. 19) and now Easton — looked ready to take a 1-0 lead halftime. But with just over 10 seconds remaining, Grant Ziervogel served a ball that Easton's Felix Valentin attempted to head away, only to watch it go into the net for a 2-0 Clippers lead.
"The own goal, miscommunication," Brice said. "We learn from it. Felix, he is an amazing defender and I told him, he's saved games prior to this. 'Don't even worry about it. It happens. It's part of the game.'"
The Warriors (6-2) thought they cut their deficit in half with 20:20 left in the game, when Clay Nagel, with Bennett keeper Jake Ziervogel away from the goal and two defenders on his back, caught up to a ball and touched it into the net. But the goal was waved off, when Nagel was ruled offsides.
"First competitive (game)," Bennett head coach Gabe Kane said. "First one that wasn't decided by halftime.
"We don't want 12 strolls," said Kane in reference to the Clippers outscoring their opponents, 53-2 this season. "We want to be battle tested, and Easton came at us for 80 minutes today. There was no quit in them. They seemed to play harder after the third goal. I think they had more chances at the end of the game when I know they were tired. But they kept battling."
Bennett bumped its lead to 3-0 as Grason Adkins scored from the right side of the box with 7:26 left.
Jake Ziervogel, who according to Kane has not had more than one save in a game this season prior to Monday, made a leaping stop on Ale Monroy with 6:45 left. Blankensop, who was recruited by a number of Division I schools but is headed to Salisbury University, just missed pushing the lead to 4-0 in the waning moments when he blasted a shot off the crossbar.
"I knew they were going to be our best opponent we'd play to date," Brice said. "I think we made some silly mistakes and we paid for them. But they are just minor ones. We switched off for a moment, not marking in the box, not getting and winning the second ball in the box.
"The score does not reflect how we played," Brice continued. "I think going forward, we work on finishing our chances and then just being a little more creative up top."

title: SSPP defeats Herons to strengthen hold on top seed for ESIAC playoffs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
SSPP defeats Herons to strengthen hold on top seed for ESIAC playoffs

 October 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 587
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — With no seniors on her team, Saints Peter and Paul High girls head soccer coach Nicole Edsall called last season a bit of a growing year.Edsall called the beginning of this season, "a bit of a rough start" after the Sabres went 2-2 over their first four games.
Now, with just one regular-season game remaining, Edsall has seen her team grow into the No. 1 seed for the approaching Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference playoffs. Buoyed by a dominating midfield, the Sabres tightened their grip on that top spot Tuesday afternoon with a 3-1 victory over Gunston for their fourth straight win, and fifth victory in six games.
"Saints Peter and Paul has a great team," said Gunston head coach Tony D'Antonio after losing to the Sabres for the second time in five days. "They're best in the conference for sure. Saints Peter and Paul's midfield was just dominant."
Edsall has literally watched that midfield grow, especially center mids Avery McCall and Annie Albright, who she has coached since fifth grade.
"Avery is just extremely athletic, can control the field," Edsall said. "And Annie's got a ton of grit and never stops running. So Annie's usually on an offensive side and Avery really controls the back and the defensive side."
Completing that midfield are seniors Gracie Galdieri and Keely Morgan.
"For the past three years they've been kind of bouncing around," Edsall said of Galdieri and Morgan. "They found homes in the outside, running the flanks. They've done a really good job doing that. They've all grown into the positions."
That group helped keep the Sabres (7-3 overall, 7-0 ESIAC) control possession, keep play largely in the Herons' end, and limited Gunston's chances on the offensive end. Adding to Sts. Peter & Paul's midfield dominance was the fact D'Antonio had his best midfielder, senior Vee McCluskey, playing goalie.
"We need her in goal," said D'Antonio, whose team lost to the Sabres 4-0 last Friday in Centreville. "Our game plan was to kind of pack things in a bit and try to attack on the transition."
That transition game materialized only a few times compared to the Sabres' attack, which struck in the 18th minute, when Kendall Kroniser crossed a ball that Albright put away in the left side of the net. Sts. Peter & Paul scored again not quite 2 minutes later, as Eden Zimmerman sent a pass across the goalmouth to Kroniser, who tapped it in for a 2-0 lead.
Gunston (5-4-1, 5-3) came close to scoring in the fourth minute of the second half on a direct kick. But Sabres keeper Kaylin Palmer tracked the ball coming in from her right side, watched it bounce through the crease, before smothering it.
Sts. Peter & Paul, which has outscored its ESIAC competition 29-4 this season, was pushing for its fourth shutout in conference play. But with 1:27 left, Gunston's Abby Philippon unloaded a 20-yard rocket from just outside the box that found the upper right corner to make it 2-1.
"That's her thing," D'Antonio said of Philippon. "She did not get a whole lot of chances today. They did a nice job. They defended very well."
The Sabres answered quickly as Eden Zimmerman converted a pass from her sister Emery Zimmerman for a goal and a 3-1 lead just 45 seconds later.
"We had a rough start to the season, but we had a tough schedule," Edsall said. "It seemed like we were losing game after game but as soon as we started the conference it clicked. So I'm thankful for the tough start to the season."

title: Queen Anne's extends North shutout streak
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's extends North shutout streak

 October 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 748
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton High's Dafny Vasquez is one of the North Bayside's more dynamic female soccer players.And Queen Anne's County junior center back Shannon Rath is well aware of those talents.
"I've played with Dafny most of my childhood, so I'm really close with her," said Rath, who used to play on the same club team with Vasquez. "I think because of that, I know just to contain and keep her in front of me, and don't let her get behind. Because if she gets behind you she's very dangerous."
Rath and her teammates kept a close eye on Vasquez Wednesday night, limiting the junior striker to just two shots, as the Lions, paced by Madi Horney's second hat trick of the season, shut out the Warriors, 6-0, for their eighth win in nine games.
"We just got done playing Colonel (Richardson) and they have Sadie Prettyman, who in my opinion is a very, very good soccer player, that we knew we had to be aware of her at all times," Queen Anne's head coach Mike Kern said. "So that's kind of what we did tonight.
"We didn't mark her up or anything," continued Kern, who had no specially designed defensive package just for Vasquez. "We just made sure we were aware of her when she did get the ball. We looked to double her, just contain her to keep her in front of us. And I think we did a good job doing that tonight because she is a very good player."
Two days after netting a hat trick against Cambridge-South Dorchester, Vazquez was limited to just two shots on goal. The first of those came in the 15th minute when she fired a strong shot from left wing that Queen Anne's keeper Bea Holthaus stopped. The Warrior standout wouldn't get another shot off until 15:21 remained in the game, when she booted a ball well over the crossbar.
"I think they always expect Dafny so they look for that double team on her," Easton head coach Ellie Kilmon said. "I think they did contain her pretty well. But we always expect it. It's just how they (Queen Anne's) work together as a team."
While the Lions (8-2 overall, 6-0 North Bayside) stifled Vasquez and Easton (6-4, 4-2), they also maintained their season-long shutout streak against division competition, blanking their seventh North opponent. Though Queen Anne's shut out Kent Island early in the season, it's next Wednesday's home game against the Buccaneers that counts toward in the division, and will determine the regular-season champion.
"Our defense has been great all year," said Kern, whose team has outscored its division opponents 49-0. "Bea in the goal has been great. Our defense is very, very good. We probably could score more goals if we didn't put so much effort in the defense."
The Lions put plenty of effort trying to score in the first half, but were either foiled by Warrior goalie Zelia Proa (10 saves), or launched shots over the crossbar.
"The first half we just couldn't get it in the net," Kern said. "So in the second half we did a better job of finishing."
Queen Anne's managed to get two in the net in the first half, the first coming with 6:48 remaining, when Horney set up Olivia Ryan's goal. The Lions made it 2-0 with 3:40 left, after Kara Ringold was taken down inside the box, setting up a penalty kick by Horney, whose shot glanced off Proa's fingertips and into the left side of the net.
Queen Anne's began widening its lead with 23:50 left in the game, when Rath's corner kick landed right at the feet of Horney, who tapped in her second goal.
Addison Chandler had a chance to put Easton on the board less than 3 minutes later, but her shot went over the crossbar.
Proa made two more saves midway through the second half before Rath struck a ball that was headed into the net by Horney, completing her hat trick for a 4-0 lead.
"I let the play come to me," Horney said. "I don't come into it cocky. I just do it."
The Lions tacked on two more goals, Ryan setting up Lexi Kern, who hit a beautiful chip from about 20 yards out that sailed over Proa and into the net with 10:31 to go, and Mia Bennett scoring with 6:30 left.
"I think we definitely have our ups and downs," Horney said. "But as of right now we're having our ups, and hopefully it keeps going coming into Kent Island next week."

title: Lions win North despite tie with Bucs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions win North despite tie with Bucs

 October 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 694
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern didn't pop out of gear or launch into a tirade.But with his team trailing and doing everything but sticking the ball in the net Wednesday night against Kent Island, Kern was a bit more animated than usual as he pleaded for more.
"I just told them we had to play harder," Kern said. "We were knocking on the doorstep the entire first half. I thought we dominated the game. We had more opportunities to score and we just couldn't get it in the net. I just told them they had to play with a little more heart."
In another physical battle that has become commonplace in this rivalry, Queen Anne's got the equalizing goal it needed, when Shannon Rath buried a penalty kick into the right side of the net in the third minute of the second half in an eventual 1-1 double-overtime tie.
While the Lions and Buccaneers each finished the regular season with identical records — 9-2-1 overall, 6-0-1 North Bayside — Queen Anne's wins the tiebreaker between the two schools based on its 1-0 victory over Kent Island on Sept. 11. Though that first meeting did not count toward the North division, it was the deciding factor since head-to-head competition is the first tiebreaker.
Queen Anne's faces two-time defending conference champion James M. Bennett (12-0) for the Bayside championship on Monday at Snow Hill High School at 6:45 p.m. It will be the fourth consecutive year the Lions and Clippers decide the conference championship. Bennett beat Queen Anne's, 3-0, on Sept. 30 in Centreville.
"I thought Olivia (Ryan) played her best game of the season," Kern said of Wednesday's clash with Kent Island. "So I think we're starting to peak a little bit. We're pretty confident. I think going against (head coach) Ed O'Leary's (Bennett) team, they know us well, we know them well. I think it's going to be a good battle.
"I think this is one of the more talented teams we've ever had," Kern continued. "I mean we can play with anybody as far from 18 to 18. We've struggled to get the ball in the back of the net against these tougher teams. But we can defend. Bennett when we played them last time, we lost 3-0, but the score didn't depict the game. We lost on the scoreboard. But we got to get the ball in the back of the net."
Queen Anne's had three direct kicks and three corner kicks in the first 17 minutes against the Bucs, but could not beat Kent Island keeper Taylor Ritz. Then with 15 minutes left in the half, Buccaneers speedster Abbie Mahaffey — with Queen Anne's Rath trying to shield her from the ball and Lions keeper Bea Holthaus moving toward the ball from the opposite direction — managed to chip a shot that floated over Holthaus for a 1-0 Kent Island lead.
"I think it was just a miscommunication," Kern said of the play. "Shannon running toward her shielding the ball, and Bea coming out. And I think Abbie just made a good play to poke a foot in there and poke it around her. It was just communication."
Kent Island, which stretched its unbeaten streak to nine games after a 1-2 start to the season, held that lead into halftime, despite the Lions swarming near the goal with less than 2 minutes left in the first half in a bid for the tying goal and Ritz away from the net. But the Bucs defense denied Queen Anne's, carrying the 1-0 lead into the break.
The Lions put immediate pressure on Kent Island early in the second half, sending a header over the crossbar. Then with almost 3 minutes elapsed, Kara Ringold was fouled just inside the box, setting up Rath, who roped a shot into the right side past Ritz's dive.
Two yellow cards against the Bucs gave Queen Anne's two more direct-kick chances, but the first sailed wide right and the second was stopped by Ritz.
The Lions came within inches of taking the lead when a shot hit under the crossbar and fell in front of the goal with 9:20 remaining in regulation.

title: Sabres finish strong on way to crown
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Sabres finish strong on way to crown

 October 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 767
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Keely Morgan's goal just 2 seconds before halftime put the home team in front.But it was Eden Zimmerman's goal off Avery McCall's beautiful corner kick that put Saints Peter and Paul High's girls soccer team finally in control.
That score gave the top-seeded Sabres an infusion of confidence Friday en route to a 4-1 victory over Gunston in the Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference championship.
"It feels amazing," said McCall, a junior midfielder, who has now been a part of conference title teams in soccer, basketball and lacrosse. "This is a very special team."
A team that had been bounced in the first round of the ESIAC postseason the past two years. A team that went undefeated in conference play this season and came in as the No. 1 seed. And a team that won its first ESIAC championship since 2019.
But the Sabres (10-3) were consistently beaten to the ball by the Herons (6-5-1) in the first half, and halfway through the second half.
"We were definitely dominant in the first half and the first 20 minutes of the second half," Gunston head coach Tony D'Antonio said. "And then it was pretty even after that. They found the net and we didn't."
Sts. Peter & Paul found the net in the 8th minute, when Emery Zimmerman parked a direct kick into the right side of the net for a 1-0 lead.
Gunston got a pair of corner kicks in the 18th minute, the first skidding through the crease but finding no one on the other end. Sabres keeper Kaylin Palmer made a save on a direct kick with 13:30 left in the first half.
The Herons then put together a flurry off a corner with 5 minutes remaining before the break. A corner kick sailed over the Palmer's outstretched fingers and through the crease. Gunston kept possession, striking a ball that hit one of its own players before sending a shot over the crossbar.
Then with 2:04 left before halftime, Ellie Roberts sent a drive from about 25 yards out that nestled into the far right corner for a 1-1 tie.
"It's hard to beat a team three times," McCall said of the Sabres' two regular-season wins over Gunston. "But I think we were mostly in panic mode. They (Gunston) always come out really fast and we're normally a second-half team. So we were very defensive and I think that's what saved us. And then eventually we got the offense together and it all came together."
Sts. Peter & Paul got a huge boost just 2 seconds before halftime when Morgan got a ball and tucked it inside the left post for a 2-1 halftime lead.
"It was absolutely huge," Sabres head coach Nicole Edsall said of Morgan's goal.
Sophomore Emery Zimmerman agreed.
"I think that was essential because it really just got us going," Emery Zimmerman said. "It (made us) realize, 'OK, we need to win this. We want to win this. This is ours. We came all this way undefeated (in conference play). This is the time that we need to come out and score.
"When they caught up to us and we got back up one more like right off the bat, it really got us going," Emery Zimmerman continued. "Gave us a lot of enthusiasm and momentum."
But not right away.
"They definitely had jitters in the first half," Edsall said of her team. "And when we talked at halftime I said, 'I know this isn't the team that we are. So just kind of brush it off. Let it go. Start the half over and let's play our game.'"
Play evened out midway through the second half. Then with 8:42 left, McCall bent a corner that plopped right in front of Eden Zimmerman, who tapped it in for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been struggling on my corners all season," McCall said. "I usually just boot it and hope. Eden is always everywhere and she just found it. It got the curve that it needed and she was just there for it. We've always been a team that struggles to like get it in (on corners). It's always gone right through. But she was just right there where she needed to be."
Less than 2 minutes later, the Sabres spilled into the box before Kendall Kroniser gained possession, spun away from a defender and drilled in a fourth goal.
"I'm sure it's great for the seniors," Emery Zimmerman said. "I'm happy for them. I feel over the last year nobody leaving (through graduation) and through this year, we really built up on our skills and built great team chemistry. And this is what happens when you work hard at practice."

title: Core's late goal lifts Bennett to third straight title
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Core's late goal lifts Bennett to third straight title

 October 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 682
 Words 

 Read News Document

 SNOW HILL — James M. Bennett High girls head soccer coach Ed O'Leary knew the final of the regular-season match was deceiving."When we beat them three-nil in Queen Anne's, we knew it wasn't a three-nil game," O'Leary said of the Clippers' Sept. 30 game with Queen Anne's County.
Monday's rematch was much different, but still the Clippers came out on the winning end, as freshman Gracie Core's goal with 3 minutes, 8 seconds remaining lifted Bennett to its third consecutive Bayside Conference championship via a 3-2 victory over the Lions at Snow Hill High's Kelly Shumate Stadium.
"We expected that from Mike (Kern) and Jeff (Anthony)," O'Leary said of Queen Anne's head coach and assistant. "First minute they just were on top, and they were so aggressive. And we like that. And they made us fight for everything. You know what? That's the way it should be."
The first half ended with Bennett (13-0) in a place it had never been all year — trailing.
With not quite 2 minutes remaining, Queen Anne's Shannon Rath drove a direct kick that Clippers keeper Sophia Valenzano (six saves) dove to her left to make an initial save on. But the ball trickled to the right of Valenzano who was still on the ground when the Lions' Kara Ringold rushed in to knock in the game's first goal.
"We came out and we ended up getting that first goal in the first half," Kern said. "It's what we needed. It was very important because we've struggled scoring against the good teams this year. We've scored a lot of goals for the season, but (in) these big games we're having a tough time putting the ball in the back of the net. So getting that first goal was huge."
Queen Anne's goalie Bea Holthaus (seven saves) kept the Lions (9-3-1) in front early in the second half when she came out to intercept a corner kick headed near her goal line. But less than 3 minutes later, Holthaus made a sliding stop on Core, who quickly possessed the rebound and dished a short pass to Rilynn East for the tying goal.
Holthaus and Valenzano each made saves on corner kick 3 minutes apart.
Bennett transitioned downfield. Core came down the right side, was bumped by Queen Anne's Hayden Legg, managed to stay on her feet, and steered a shot past Holthaus into the left side for a 2-1 Bennett lead with 20:41 remaining in the game.
"Bennett's a strong team and we defended them well for most of the game," said Kern of a Clippers team that had outscored the opposition 82-3 this season.
Queen Anne's wasn't quite through though.
With 11:10 left, Madison Horney carried into the box, stumbled slightly through a tackle by Bennett's Taylor Matthews, then while falling, managed to get enough of her right foot on the ball to get it past Valenzano for a 2-2 tie. It was the first time Bennett had allowed two goals in game all season.
"We came back, hung tough," Kern said.
Queen Anne's came within inches of taking a lead when it banged shot off a corner went off the crossbar with 6:22 remaining.
The game appeared headed for overtime. But with the clock approaching the 3-minute mark, Core collected a ball that glanced off a defender, and from right wing, drove a left-footed shot into the left side of the net for the winning goal.
"I hope the crowd enjoyed it because it was a wonderful game," O'Leary said. "We got a little bit lucky in the end. They could have scored but the crossbar. But our super freshman (Core) went and scored a cracking goal at the end."
It was the Lions third straight loss to the Clippers in the championship game, yet Kern — who told his team afterwards "This was better than any practice we could have had," came away encouraged.
"Hit the crossbar on a corner kick and we had bad clear in the back and they capitalized on it," Kern said. "Proud of the girls. Proud how they played. The effort was there. And I think we can build from it moving into the playoffs."

title: Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004

 November 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 618
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Lexi Kern was going to get a turn regardless."The whole team knows Lexi does well with PKs," Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern said of his daughter.
Coach Kern sent his 11 players onto the field for a shootout to decide last Friday's Class 2A state quarterfinal against Wilde Lake, but noticed his third and fourth shooters had bumped themselves further back in the lineup. After Shannon Rath and Morgan Scott each buried their PKs, Kern watched his daughter move into the third spot and step behind the ball.
"She said, 'OK, I'll go,'" the coach said.
Like Rath and Scott, Lexi Kern parked her PK in the right corner, then watched Wilde Lake's third attempt miss the mark, sealing a 1-0 victory that gave the Lions their first state semifinal berth since 2004.
Second-seeded Queen Anne's (12-3-1) advances to Saturday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet No. 3 seed Century (12-2-1) at 2:30 p.m. at Kent Island High School in Stevensville.
"That was kind of a cool moment for me," Mike Kern said of Lexi's PK. "Nobody else wanted it, which is the crazy part. Lexi is usually four or five or six (in the PK lineup). They just did not want to take it."
The Lions followed a familiar pattern against the seventh-seeded Wildecats (7-6-3), dominating play without benefit of a goal — though one score was negated by a questionable offsides call.
After two overtime periods, the game moved into penalty kicks.
"I was surprised how calm I was," said Mike Kern, who noted an eerie quiet fell over Lions Stadium during the shootout. "It was like golf. You could hear a pin drop. Both teams. After they made them they cheered. But it was quiet as could be. I had never experienced anything like that."
Queen Anne's went first, with Rath driving a shot into the right side of the net. Wilde Lake's first PK sailed over the crossbar.
Celebrating her 18th birthday, Scott deposited her PK in nearly the exact same spot at Rath's shot. The Wildecats' second attempt went wide. Lexi Kern promptly booted her shot into the right corner for a 3-0 lead. Wilde Lake's third — and final chance — again went well over the head of Lions keeper Bea Holthaus and the crossbar, clinching the victory.
This is the Lions' third trip to the state semifinals under their 24-year head coach. Queen Anne's last reached the state semis as a 1A school in 2004, when it lost in the closing minute of double overtime to Tuscarora. Queen Anne's also reached the state semifinals in 2003, outlasting Oakland Mills in an 11-man shootout before falling in the state final.
Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have built solid teams in the past, but often were eliminated by 2A powers Fallston and Bel Air.
But this season, Kern thought he had the goods to make a return trip to the final four.
"I really thought this team had the chance to get there," Kern said. "I think they're competitors. They love to compete. Even at practice with each other, they don't like to lose. And I think they accept challenges. They've been together for so long and played together for a long time. And I think they feed off each other. I think that they're competitors is the biggest thing."
Queen Anne's has posted 10 shutouts this season, and now faces a Century program that won the state title just two years ago. Since losing their first two games of the season by a combined score of 7-0, the Knights have gone 12-0-1 and logged 11 shutouts, including 10 straight.
"They very defensive," Kern said of the Knights. "They are very similar to us. I think we've got a legitimate shot."

title: STATE CHAMPS
author: Bill Haufe
content:
STATE CHAMPS

 November 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1085

 Read News Document

 BALTIMORE — Mike Kern's belief never wavered.From the beginning of the season, Queen Anne's County High's girls head soccer coach said his team could compete for a state title. Kern said it after wins. He seemed more emphatic after losses. He continued saying it one narrow postseason victory after another.
"We just have to put the ball in the back of the net," Kern said.
Kara Ringold did that twice early Saturday afternoon as Queen Anne's shut out C. Milton Wright, 2-0, to win the Class 2A state championship at Loyola University's Ridley Athletic Complex.
It was the first state title in the history of Queen Anne's girls soccer program, and the first by a Bayside Conference school since the Maryland Public Secondary School Athletic Association began holding the girls state championship in 1989.
"At the beginning of the season our goal was to get to a state championship," said Kern, who has been the Lions head coach for 24 years. "To win it, this is like a bonus. We knew we had the team."
Whether it was early-game jitters or the strong winds that whipped across the field, neither team mounted much offense through the first 12 minutes. C. Milton Wright (12-5), which was playing into the wind during the first half, had two early chances, the first coming on a corner kick 5 minutes in that produced no shot. Then with 28:30 left in the half, Emma Jankowiak broke in alone only to have Queen Anne's Finley Patchett angle in to take the ball away.
"I think the first half, playing into the wind, that was really difficult," Mustangs head coach Andrew Harrell said. "It was probably the toughest conditions we've played with all season. We've played with a little bit of drizzle, we've played with cold, we played with hot. But the wind is something we've never played with. And it's definitely a game-changer, especially in the first half. Playing into the wind, it's like you're playing against an extra person."
Queen Anne's (14-3-1) ended the scoreless duel more than 14 minutes later.
Shannon Rath struck a beautiful ball on a direct kick toward the center of the goal that C.M. Wright's Nani Milich headed. The ball drifted toward the right post. Mustangs goalie Alix Bramble moved to her left in an attempt to knock the ball away. But Queen Anne's Morgan Scott headed the ball back across the crease to an ummarked Ringold, who got her right foot on the ball for a tap-in and a 1-0 lead with 14 minutes, 47 seconds left in the first half.
"Shannon hit a great ball and then Morgan got a head on it and I just hit it right in," Ringold said.
The Lions, who won their state quarterfinal and semifinal on penalty kicks, scored in regulation for the first time since their 2-0 victory over Kent Island on Oct. 29 in the Class 2A East Region II final.
"I think it gave us all a lot of comfort because we have been trying to get that goal in regulation," Queen Anne's senior midfielder Olivia Ryan said. "And we ended up getting another one. But we wanted to at least get one. So it gave us a lot of comfort and we all could relax a little bit, but still have the momentum to keep going."
The fifth-seeded Mustangs got a corner kick with 51 seconds left in the first half, and then back-to-back corners in the opening 4 minutes of the second half, but put nothing on Lions sophomore keeper Bea Holthaus, who notched her 12th shutout of the season.
"Our goalie saved our butt a lot of times this season," Ryan said of Holthaus, who after giving up a goal in the regional semifinals posted four straight shutouts to end the season.
Having a stellar defense also helped.
"A lot of us have played together since we were very little so we kind of know each other's habits," senior center back Shannon Rath said. "That definitely helps a lot. Our communication is what gets us through. We are constantly talking, tracking down runners. That's just the only way we know how to do it."
Ten minutes after the Mustangs' second corner of the half, Queen Anne's put together another score.
Mia Barnette came down left wing and touched the ball to Taylor Napier, who pushed toward the middle of the field and dished to Ringold. With two defenders in front of her, and a third closing in from the left, Ringold settled the ball then quickly drove a left-footed shot inside the right post for a 2-0 lead with 26:05 left in the game.
"We were just on an attack and then we had really good passing on the left side, and Taylor (Napier) played me a great ball and I just took a touch around the defender and hoped for the best, and it went in," Ringold said. "it was just one of the best moments of my life.
"Kara was in the right place at the right time that first goal," Kerr said. "But that second goal, she earned that goal. There was a lot of things that led up to it. But when she got the ball she had to do a couple things there to get a good shot off and put it far post, low."
C.M. Wright got a shot off from outside the box that Holthaus caught in the midsection with 13:39 left, then sent a corner kick through the box and out of bounds with 6:37 left. The Mustangs didn't build a serious scoring threat the rest of the game.
"I think when you get to this stage, you watch enough game film to come up with a game plan for the other team," Harrell said. "But what you can't game plan for is the work ethic and the hard work and that kind of stuff. And I think Queen Anne's brought a ton of intensity and a lot of hard work today. They beat us to balls for the majority of the game. That was one of our halftime talks; we got to do better getting to the ball first."
It was Queen Anne's first state finals appearance since 2003, when it lost 2-0 to Loch Raven.
"I felt like last year we had the team," Kern said. "We did get some injuries at the end of the year and things didn't go our way. But we had a good core of the group back and thought this was going to be the year for us. Everything just kind of fell into place for us."
